Code Repositories.section: Code and Data Availability, printed pages14–15
Code Repositories.evidence: The paper identifies github.com/carter-yagemann/recon2026-semantic-shields as the public repository containing primary scripts and the ransom-note artifacts used in the experiment. Methods section3, printed page7, identifies295 notes from189 actors obtained through ransomlook.io.

removed_tag_reasons.Public Records: Publicly downloadable ransom-note artifacts are not established as public records; the explicitly identified code/data repository is the supported source category.
removed_tag_reasons.News Media: The methods/data-availability sections do not identify news reporting as a study source.
removed_tag_reasons.Forums & Communities: The methods/data-availability sections identify a ransom-note collection and public code/data repository, not a forum/community dataset.
removed_tag_reasons.Leaked Data: Ransom notes are not evidence that victim leaked data was used; no such dataset is established in the inspected methods.
